evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","due":"2026-10-31"} returned 201 and the todo had due "2026-10-31". A POST without due returned 201 with due null. The date is a YYYY-MM-DD string with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 with {"due":"2026-10-01"} returned 200 and set the due date. PATCH with {"due":null} returned 200 and due became null. Setting a date again also worked.
evidence.AC3: POST with due "2026-02-30", "01.02.2026", "2026-13-01" and the number 20260101 each returned 400 with 'due must be a YYYY-MM-DD date'. PATCH with "2026-02-30" and "bad" also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-11-01 UTC. I created todos with due 10-31 (past), 11-01 (today), 12-01 (future), none, and a past one that I then marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past undone todo and the one with a changed past due date. Today's, future, no-due and done todos were excluded, and their overdue flag was false in GET /todos.
evidence.AC5: The list page at / showed each due date next to its todo: 'past 31.10.2026', 'today 01.11.2026', 'future 01.12.2026', 'nodue 01.10.2026', 'pastdone ✓ 01.01.2026'.
evidence.AC6: On the list page, 'past 31.10.2026 überfällig' and 'nodue 01.10.2026 überfällig' (due date set to the past) carried the word. The today, future and done-with-past-due todos did not.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only the two overdue todos, 'past' and 'nodue'.
